analysis:
Examined both inference excerpts, Autopilot metadata, the full supplied Autopilot patch and its BASE text. The only inference change is docs/architecture/inference.md:2371: placement holds exclude idle slots from eviction and reclaim credit. Surrounding native ownership, media, prefix-cache, cancellation and Flint output contracts are unchanged; they do not establish a new encryption, disclosure or authorization regression (T-008, T-010, T-041, T-053).
The Autopilot documentation now describes expanded cached-model eligibility, default-enabled downloads under saved consent, persistent download records, lease-independent adoption, expiring holds and transition supervision (docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md, head patch lines 37–255). These materially expand documented resource/control behavior but are not executable evidence of a vulnerability. Documented safeguards include catalog/hash verification, runtime and load-budget checks, a 256-ID set bound, disk reserve, consent rechecks and preservation of ownership fences. No supplied change touches keys, attestation grants, billing or cache cryptography.
Integration must examine AutopilotModelSet/AutopilotStartInventory, ProviderLoop+AutopilotDownload and AutopilotDownloadLedger for actual hash/consent enforcement, concurrent disk-budget accounting and limit/disable changes during transfers; reconcile adoption/hold termination with serving authorization and retirement in ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement and resolveStalledTransition. Verify that the new remote download and persistent placement contracts are represented in the threat model's TB-002/TB-007 availability scope (including T-016/T-029), without treating model adoption as A-016 authorization. The consent UI/migration contract is not supplied, so this pass cannot conclude whether existing consent authorizes the broader behavior. Source absence is a coverage limit, not proof of missing controls; these material questions require the implementation integration pass.
